analysis.title: FSA Fixed Income Daily Commentary - 10 November 2026
key_insights: Treasuries bear-flattened on Monday. The 2-year rose 5 bps to 4.56% and the 30-year rose 1 bp to 5.28%. Drivers cited were post-midterm buying, strong October jobs data, a solid 3-year auction and lower oil.
Fed funds futures imply an 84.1% probability of a 25 bp hike at the December 9, 2026 FOMC meeting, up from roughly 75% earlier in the week.

Goolsbee (Chicago Fed) and Barkin (Richmond Fed) both leaned hawkish. Goolsbee flagged overheating risk from the AI buildout and broadening inflation. Barkin said policy direction is higher but any further hikes should come at a careful pace.
The Treasury sold $58 billion of 3-year notes at 4.627%, tailing the when-issued level by 0.5 bp. Primary dealers took only 9.5%, direct bidders 35% and indirect bidders 55.5%.

Brent and WTI settled at their lowest since August 2026 on US-Iran diplomacy. A reported Qatari and Pakistani-mediated framework would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, limit Iranian enrichment and release Iranian assets.

China extends the suspension of an additional 24% tariff on US imports for two months from November 10 while keeping a 10% tariff. The suspension of port fees on US-linked vessels runs to January 10, 2027.
China PPI rose 5.7% YoY in October, the fastest since June 2022, while CPI slowed to 0.7% and core CPI fell to 0.8%. Producers are struggling to pass costs on to households.
NY Fed survey inflation expectations were unchanged at 3.9% (1-year), 3.3% (3-year) and 3.0% (5-year). Expected unemployment rose to 45.3%, the highest since April 2020.

Barrick Mining upgraded to OP from MP on 3Q26 results. Adjusted EBITDA was up 22% YoY at a 60% margin, net cash was USD909 million, no debt principal is due before 2031 and 2026 capex guidance was cut. Gold AISC rose to USD1,911/oz. Preference is for its 2035 paper.

Mirae Asset Securities cut to MP from OP after cyberattacks on November 4 and 5 exposed data of 35,255 employees and contractors and about 3,800 customer account numbers. Immediate financial impact looks limited but operational-risk concerns rise.
Suntec REIT upgraded to OP from MP. Distributable income rose 14.3% and DPU rose 13.4%, helped by Singapore office leasing and lower funding costs. Leverage rose to 43.0% and debt maturity shortened.

ORIX 2QFY27 net income of JPY575.39 billion beat consensus, but the beat came mostly from non-recurring gains including Kioxia (JPY417 billion in the quarter). Revenue was up only 0.2% YoY and FY27 net income guidance was held at JPY530 billion, implying a second-half reversal. Rated MP.

SoftBank Corp. 2QFY27 beat on net income and sales, raised FY27 guidance, and saw ARPU rise to JPY3,950. Net leverage rose to 2.8x and adjusted FCF fell. Rated MP, with the 2035 paper preferred over the 2030.

SoftBank Group stays MP. OpenAI reportedly shrank its round to at least a third smaller at a $1.25 trillion valuation, with SoftBank in talks to invest only hundreds of millions. China's security review blocked SoftBank's $5.4 billion ABB Robotics deal. The preference is the front end of the curve.

KKR 3Q26 fee related earnings of USD1.32 billion and adjusted net income of USD1.78 per share beat estimates. AUM of USD804 billion missed the USD815 billion estimate. Net cash and investments is USD5 billion and the buyback was raised by USD500 million. Rated MP.

Occidental 3Q26 cut principal debt by USD1.8 billion to USD10.0 billion and raised free cash flow before working capital to USD2,779 million. Net debt is USD7,946 million. The desk expects an upgrade to full IG and stays OP.

Paramount (Skydance) gross debt rose to USD87 billion after the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closed. S&P and Fitch both cut to BB. The desk calls the results credit neutral, stays MP and says SKYD papers already price a further downgrade.
Ma'aden Q3 was credit negative. EBITDA fell 24% as phosphate EBITDA fell 83% on sulfur costs, offset by record aluminum and gold. FY26 capex guidance was cut by $1bn. Rated MP.

Mercedes-Benz was cut to A- from A by S&P on 6 November with a negative outlook. Q3 adjusted EBIT fell 15% and Cars' adjusted EBIT fell 51% on a 31% drop in China deliveries. Cars' FY26 return on sales guidance was cut to 2-3%. Rated MP with downside rating risk.

Braskem restructuring suffered a setback as bondholders rejected a plan to convert USD3.8bn of debt into equity, and Petrobras and IG4 withdrew a conditional USD1.4bn capital injection. A contentious judicial restructuring is more likely before the late-November deadline. Rated MP, cautious.

CSN agreed to sell CSN Cimentos to Huaxin for an enterprise value of BRL12.7bn, below earlier hopes of at least BRL15bn. Reported leverage would fall from 3.5x to about 2.8x, but adjusted leverage only from 5.15x to 4.64x. Credit positive but not a turnaround.

WE Soda is restructuring its Wyoming operations, which cuts annual US sales by over 1.5mt. It sold off sharply, with the 2028s near 94 and the 2031s near 87-88. Rated MP, favouring the 2031s over the 2028s.
Turkcell Q3 beat consensus on revenue, EBITDA and net income. Net leverage is 0.31x but the net short FX position is USD1.3bn. Rated MP.
JBS 3Q adjusted EBITDA fell 35.6% to US$1.18bn and net leverage rose to 3.54x from 2.39x. Free cash flow turned negative. Rated MP and on close monitor.

Rating agency actions: S&P upgraded AB InBev to A from A- and the desk calls it priced in (MP). Fitch placed CVS on Rating Watch Positive ahead of the pharmacy spin-off (MP). Moody's moved Alstom's Baa3 outlook to negative (MP). Fitch cut Goodyear to B+ and the CEO stepped down (UP).
Nordea was acquitted on 5 of 7 counts in the Copenhagen AML case and fined DKK155 million, 2.3% of the claim. CET1 is 15.8%, 1.9pp above the requirement. Credit neutral, MP.

Other credit-neutral updates, all MP unless noted: Crédit Agricole's friendly proposal to merge Banco BPM with Crédit Agricole Italia, Lendlease's lost MSG North sale, Carlsberg's sale of Britvic Brazil, Karoon's Brazil export tax extension, Hidrovias 3Q, CMPC 3Q, New Zealand's preliminary election count. Goodman (OP) bought half of a 9.9% NEXTDC stake.

Singapore REITs and managers stay OP. LREIT shows 10.0% retail rental reversion and 2.1x regulatory interest coverage. CapitaLand Investment fee-related revenue rose 15% over nine months, helped by event-driven fees.
TSMC is reportedly drafting plans for 3D DRAM at Nvidia's request but has not confirmed. The desk flags capex and cyclicality as the credit issue and stays MP.

market_movers.rationale: Moved to OP from MP after 3Q26 showed adjusted EBITDA up 22%, net cash of USD909 million and no debt principal due before 2031. Prefers the 2035 paper.
Mirae Asset Securities cut to MP from OP after the November 4-5 cyberattacks raised operational-risk and governance concerns.
Suntec REIT moved to OP from MP on 14.3% higher distributable income and lower funding costs, though leverage rose to 43.0%.
MP on TSMC. The reported 3D DRAM plan is strategically positive but could raise capex and cyclicality.
MP on ORIX at fair valuations. The 2QFY27 beat was driven by Kioxia and disposal gains while revenue was flat.
MP on SoftBank Corp. Results are credit positive but net leverage is 2.8x. Prefers the 2035 paper over the 2030.
MP on SoftBank Group. OpenAI exposure is a valuation risk rather than a default risk. Prefers the front end of the curve.
MP. Fee related earnings and adjusted net income beat, with net cash and an undrawn USD3 billion revolver.
OP. Principal debt is cut to USD10.0 billion. The desk expects an upgrade to full IG in the coming quarters.
MP. Credit neutral results, gross debt USD87 billion. Bonds already price a further downgrade.
Hidrovias MP. Net debt to EBITDA of 2.3x against a 3.5x covenant, volumes eased in two corridors.
Nordea MP. Acquitted on 5 of 7 AML counts, fine of DKK155 million, CET1 15.8%.
Lendlease MP. Lost AUD90 million sale proceeds and possible AUD160 million funding need, against AUD3,957 million of liquidity.
UP. CEO stepped down days after 3Q26, Fitch cut to B+, free cash flow was negative USD283 million in the quarter.
Crédit Agricole MP. Friendly merger proposal for Banco BPM, credit neutral.
Carlsberg MP. The EUR80 million Britvic Brazil sale is small against DKK56.8 billion of net debt.
Karoon MP. Export tax extended to December 31, 2026, unchanged guidance.
Goodman OP. Gearing of 6.5% leaves room to absorb its half of a 9.9% NEXTDC stake.
New Zealand sovereign MP. Preliminary count gives National, ACT and NZ First 67 seats against 66 needed.
CMPC MP. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 4.23x. Asset sales of USD420 million and USD365.5 million carry the credit.
AB InBev MP. The S&P upgrade to A was largely expected and priced in. Prefers intermediate maturities.
MP. Fitch put the ratings on Rating Watch Positive ahead of the CVS Pharmacy spin-off, expected in 1H28.
Alstom MP. Moody's outlook moved to negative after guidance cuts, with ample cash of EUR1.65 billion.
Ma'aden MP. Phosphate pressure outweighed record aluminum and gold, capex guidance cut by $1bn.
Mercedes-Benz MP despite the S&P downgrade to A-. Downside rating risk remains until profitability and FCF recover.
CSN MP. Cement disposal is balance-sheet relief rather than a turnaround. Adjusted leverage stays high.
Braskem MP with a cautious view. Bondholders rejected the debt-for-equity plan and shareholder funding was withdrawn.
WE Soda MP. Favours the 2031s over the 2028s. Refinancing is the main concern.
Turkcell MP. Q3 beat consensus, but FX exposure and 5G capex limit further credit improvement.
JBS MP on close monitor. Net leverage rose to 3.54x and free cash flow turned negative.
Lendlease Global Commercial REIT OP. High retail occupancy and positive reversions, with 2.1x regulatory coverage.
CapitaLand Investment OP. Higher operating cash flow and lower borrowing costs, though event-driven fees inflated fee growth.

sector_views.rationale: Barrick upgraded to OP on net cash, no principal due before 2031 and cut capex guidance.
Suntec, LREIT and CapitaLand Investment all rated OP on leasing strength and lower funding costs, with leverage and rate sensitivity noted.
CSN disposal is relief but not a turnaround, and Braskem restructuring talks deteriorated.
Mercedes-Benz stays MP but with downside rating risk from China weakness and pricing pressure.

earnings_insights: ORIX 2QFY27 reported net income JPY575.39 billion vs consensus est JPY507.2 billion (reported 11/9). Adjusted net income excluding Kioxia gains was JPY317,529 million. Revenue JPY797.25 billion, +0.2% YoY. FY27 net income guidance held at JPY530 billion.

SoftBank Corp. 2QFY27 reported net income JPY214.48 billion vs est JPY199.36 billion. Operating income JPY339.84 billion vs est JPY339.15 billion. Net sales JPY1.98 trillion vs est JPY1.87 trillion. FY27 operating income guidance raised to JPY1.16 trillion from JPY1.10 trillion and net income guidance to JPY610 billion from JPY560 billion.

KKR 3Q26 reported fee related earnings USD1.32 billion (+27% YoY) vs est USD1.26 billion. Adjusted net income USD1.78 per adjusted share vs consensus USD1.63. AUM USD804 billion vs est USD815 billion. Total revenues USD4.56 billion, -17% YoY.

Barrick 3Q26 reported revenue USD5,073 million (+22% YoY). Adjusted net earnings USD0.82 per share vs consensus USD0.78. Attributable adjusted EBITDA USD2,475 million. 2026 capex guidance cut to USD3.8-4.2 billion. Gold and copper guidance kept.

Occidental 3Q26 reported net income USD1,637 million vs USD661 million in 3Q25. Adjusted income USD1,951 million vs USD513 million. Production 1,427 Mboed, above the midpoint of 1,400-1,440 Mboed guidance. 4Q guidance 1,430-1,470 Mboed.

Paramount 3Q26 reported revenue USD7,025 million (+5% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA USD1.0 billion vs USD997 million pro forma. Parent net earnings USD73 million. Free cash flow USD31 million. 2026 standalone guidance kept, with the film slate expected to hit 4Q profit by up to USD200 million.
Hidrovias 3Q26 reported operating revenue BRL653 million (-8% YoY). Recurring adjusted EBITDA BRL303 million (-16% YoY). Net profit BRL79 million vs BRL90 million in 3Q25.

Mercedes-Benz Q3 2026 reported revenue EUR30.7bn (-5% YoY). Reported EBIT EUR1.77bn (+136%). Adjusted EBIT EUR1.78bn (-15%). Industrial FCF EUR172mn vs EUR1.37bn. FY26 Cars adjusted return on sales guidance cut to 2-3% from 3-5%.

Turkcell Q3 2026 reported revenue TRY82.0bn (+6.2% YoY real), EBITDA TRY36.2bn (+6.8%), net income TRY6.7bn (-3.8%). Beat consensus by 2.7%, 8.2% and 25.5% respectively. EBITDA margin 44.2% vs 41.9% expected.
JBS 3Q reported net sales US$22.74bn (+0.6% YoY). IFRS adjusted EBITDA US$1.18bn (-35.6%), margin 5.2% vs 8.1%. Net income US$164m vs US$581m.
Ma'aden Q3/26 reported revenue $3.0bn (+11% YoY), EBITDA $0.9bn (-24%). Phosphate EBITDA $135m (-83%). Aluminum EBITDA $419m (+108%). Gold EBITDA $403m (+71%).
Suntec REIT quarter to 30 September 2026 reported gross revenue S$123.6m (+5.2% YoY), NPI S$83.4m (+6.2%), distributable income S$59.9m (+14.3%), DPU 2.017 Singapore cents (+13.4%).
CapitaLand Investment 9M 2026 reported revenue about S$1.5bn (-3% YoY). Fee-related revenue S$1.04bn (+15%). Real estate investment revenue S$580m (-23%).
CMPC 3Q26 reported sales USD1,932 million (+4% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA USD252 million (-3% YoY). Net loss USD7.2 million vs profit USD33.8 million a year earlier.

Hidrovias, Karoon, Carlsberg, Nordea and CSN items in this note are corporate events or prior-quarter figures and not new earnings prints, except Nordea's third-quarter net profit of EUR1,181 million, which was reported 10/15.

trade_ideas.rationale: Net cash, no principal due before 2031, free cash flow up 127% QoQ.

risk_factors: A December Fed hike is priced at 84.1%, with hawkish Fed speakers pointing to inflation risk from the AI buildout and energy cost pass-through.
A US-Iran deal could fail, reversing the oil decline, and a Hormuz reopening is still only a reported framework.
A weaker AI funding environment (OpenAI round shrunk, SoftBank commitment reduced) could weigh on tech and on SoftBank's portfolio marks.
Braskem faces a more contentious judicial restructuring ahead of the late-November deadline and a separate US bankruptcy filing by holders of its 2041 notes.
Paramount's leverage after the Warner Bros. Discovery deal (gross debt USD87 billion, 5.50x covenant cap) leaves further downgrade risk.
China weakness is hitting Mercedes-Benz (China deliveries -31%) and AB InBev.
Phosphate sulfur costs and regional supply-chain risks pressure Ma'aden.
Refinancing risk for WE Soda (USD980mn of 2028 bonds) and a shorter debt maturity profile at Suntec REIT.
Chinese regulatory screening can derail cross-border M&A, as with ABB Robotics.
Mirae Asset Securities faces possible regulatory penalties and client attrition after the cyberattack.
geopolitical: President Trump said further US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely and declared Iran militarily effectively over after meeting the Qatari prime minister.
Al Arabiya reported the US and Iran may be close to a Qatari- and Pakistani-mediated deal covering reopening the Strait of Hormuz, limits on enrichment and release of Iranian assets.
China extends the suspension of an additional 24% tariff on specified US imports for two months from November 10 and keeps a 10% tariff, extending the Busan trade truce.
China's foreign-investment security-review mechanism blocked SoftBank's $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB Robotics, and the parties are exploring a carve-out of the Chinese business.
China's State Council pledged stronger stock market stability and capital-market stabilisation mechanisms and will plan 2027 policy priorities.
Brazil extended its temporary tax on crude oil exports to December 31, 2026.
New Zealand's general election preliminary count shows National, ACT and NZ First with 67 seats against 66 needed, with official results due November 27.
